key_insight: A single equivalent-circuit model can jointly explain the photoluminescence and electrical behavior of valley photovoltaic devices, revealing that a reverse diode drives the observed S-shaped I–V response.
engineering_relevance: Designing high-efficiency valley photovoltaic devices requires eliminating the reverse-diode pathway that blocks carrier extraction and suppresses performance.
method: Measured intensity- and voltage-dependent photoluminescence alongside electrical I–V responses.
Built an equivalent-circuit model that fits the S-shaped current-voltage curves and the optical/electrical signals together.
Used Poisson/drift-diffusion simulations to test whether the reverse diode arises from valley scattering or a heterojunction barrier.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the combined model matches the measured photoluminescence and electrical data and explains the device's low-efficiency S-shaped I–V behavior.
watch_item: The inferred reverse diode must be removed before the approach can translate into high-efficiency VPV devices, and its physical origin may depend on material or junction design.
paper_title: Combined photoluminescence and electrical characterization of valley photovoltaic devices explained with an equivalent circuit
